## stats.kt { #stats-kt }

Descriptive statistics, and the SVG/HTML renderings Field uses to put them in a box output.

[`buildSummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt--buildsummarystats) reduces a sequence of doubles to a [`SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-summarystats) — count, quartiles, IQR,
MAD, variance, skewness, excess kurtosis — dropping and counting non-finite values as it goes.
[`buildHistogram`](math.md#stats-kt--buildhistogram) picks a bin width as the smallest of the Freedman–Diaconis, Scott and Sturges
estimates, clamped to at most 2000 bins. [`SummaryStatsBuffer`](math.md#stats-kt-summarystatsbuffer) wraps both behind a synchronized,
capped sliding window you can `add` to sample by sample; there are parallel
[`Vec2SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-vec2summarystats) / [`Vec3SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-vec3summarystats) / [`Vec4SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-vec4summarystats) forms that carry per-component
stats, vector length and the pairwise component correlations, each with their own buffer.

The rendering half — [`histogramToSvg`](math.md#stats-kt--histogramtosvg), [`seriesPlotToSvg`](math.md#stats-kt--seriesplottosvg) and [`summaryStatsBoxToHtml`](math.md#stats-kt--summarystatsboxtohtml) — builds
SVG and HTML by string interpolation, with no drawing library involved, and defaults to
Field's cyan-on-black look through a long list of colour and padding parameters. Pass the
previous [`SummaryStats`](math.md#stats-kt-summarystats) and changed numbers are tinted by the sign and relative size of the
change. [`seriesPlotToSvg`](math.md#stats-kt--seriesplottosvg) envelope-downsamples to `maxSeriesPoints` (500) before drawing.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/math/statistics/stats.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/stats/)

## timeseries.kt { #timeseries-kt }

Streaming, time-domain filters over `Float` signals — the sample-at-a-time counterpart to the
frequency-domain code in `spectral.kt`.

Everything here implements the [`FloatFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-floatfilter) fun interface (one `Float` in, one `Float` out)
and composes with `then`, so a chain reads as
`DCBlocker() then EMAFilter(0.1f) then NoiseGate(0.05f)`. Three families share that interface:
smoothers and classic filters ([`EMAFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-emafilter), [`AlphaBetaFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-alphabetafilter), [`OneEuroFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-oneeurofilter), [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter)
with its [`LowPassFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--lowpassfilter) / [`HighPassFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--highpassfilter) / [`BandPassFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--bandpassfilter) / [`BandRejectFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--bandrejectfilter)
constructors); rolling distribution fits — exponential, gamma, beta and Rayleigh — each
paired with a `Normalizer` mapping the fitted CDF into a target range and an `EventDetector`
firing on tail probability ([`ZScoreEventDetector`](math.md#timeseries-kt-zscoreeventdetector) instead thresholds on standard deviations
from a rolling mean); and utility stages such as [`MedianFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-medianfilter), [`SchmittTrigger`](math.md#timeseries-kt-schmitttrigger), [`AGC`](math.md#timeseries-kt-agc),
[`PIDController`](math.md#timeseries-kt-pidcontroller), [`LeakyIntegrator`](math.md#timeseries-kt-leakyintegrator) and [`DynamicRangeCompressor`](math.md#timeseries-kt-dynamicrangecompressor).

Pure Kotlin with no external dependency: the log-gamma, regularized incomplete gamma and
regularized incomplete beta functions the distribution fits need are implemented privately at
the top of this file. Filters are stateful objects, so use one instance per signal, and the
window-based ones allocate their ring buffer up front from `windowSize`.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/math/statistics/timeseries.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/)

**Used in:** [Signal examples: time and frequency](../spectral_examples.md)

Higher [`q`](math.md#timeseries-kt--biquadfilter--q) gives a narrower notch; this is `BiquadType.NOTCH` under a friendlier name. |

### FloatFilter { #timeseries-kt-floatfilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">fun</span> <span class="k">interface</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L299)

One `Float` in, one `Float` out — the shape every filter in this file takes, and the reason they chain. A filter is a stateful object called once per sample, in arrival order: it is not a pure function, and calling it is what advances its state, so never call one twice on the same sample just to read a number back out of it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |

| <a id="timeseries-kt--floatfilter--then"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">infix</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">then</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">next</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L310) | Series composition, left to right: `a then b` feeds `a`'s output into `b`, so `DCBlocker() then EMAFilter(0.1f)` takes the offset out first and smooths what is left. |

### EMAFilter { #timeseries-kt-emafilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">EMAFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L325)

Exponential moving average — the cheapest useful smoother, `out = alpha * in + (1 - alpha) * out`. One multiply-add and one field of state, which is why it is so often the first thing in a chain.

### AlphaBetaFilter { #timeseries-kt-alphabetafilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AlphaBetaFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dt</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L354)

A constant-velocity tracker with fixed gains — a Kalman filter's structure without its bookkeeping. It carries a position *and* a velocity, predicts one step ahead, then corrects both from the residual, so unlike [`EMAFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-emafilter) it keeps up with a steadily moving signal instead of trailing behind it.

### OneEuroFilter { #timeseries-kt-oneeurofilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">OneEuroFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">minCutoff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">dCutoff</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="o">?</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">null</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L395)

The 1€ filter (Casiez, Roussel & Vogel): a low-pass whose cutoff rises with the signal's own speed, so a slow-moving hand gets smoothed hard while a fast gesture is barely delayed. The usual pick for pointer, touch or tracker input, where lag is more objectionable than jitter.

| <a id="timeseries-kt--oneeurofilter--beta"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How strongly measured speed raises the cutoff: `cutoff = minCutoff + beta * \|speed\|`. At 0 the adaptation is off and this is an ordinary one-pole low-pass at [`minCutoff`](math.md#timeseries-kt--oneeurofilter--mincutoff). |

Raise it if the adaptation feels sluggish, lower it if noise in the speed makes the cutoff jitter. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--oneeurofilter--samplerate"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="o">?</span></code> | The rate in Hz the samples were taken at. When set, `dt` is `1 / sampleRate` on every call; when `null`, `dt` is measured from the wall clock between calls. |

### BiquadType { #timeseries-kt-biquadtype }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">enum</span> <span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">BiquadType</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L458)

Which of the RBJ audio-EQ-cookbook shapes a [`BiquadFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt-biquadfilter) realises. `LOWPASS`, `HIGHPASS`, `BANDPASS` and `NOTCH` are determined entirely by frequency and Q; `PEAK`, `LOWSHELF` and `HIGHSHELF` are the only three that read `gainDb` — the others accept it and ignore it.

Constants: `LOWPASS`, `HIGHPASS`, `BANDPASS`, `NOTCH`, `PEAK`, `LOWSHELF`, `HIGHSHELF`.

### BiquadFilter { #timeseries-kt-biquadfilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BiquadFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">type</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">BiquadType</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">frequency</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">q</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.707f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">gainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L475)

A second-order IIR section — two poles, two zeros — run as a direct-form I recursion with coefficients from the RBJ audio-EQ cookbook. This is the machinery behind [`LowPassFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--lowpassfilter), [`HighPassFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--highpassfilter), [`BandPassFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--bandpassfilter) and [`BandRejectFilter`](math.md#timeseries-kt--bandrejectfilter), and what to reach for when you want a filter with an actual corner frequency rather than a vague smoothing coefficient.

Run once at construction; run it again yourself after mutating any of those, because nothing else will. It leaves the delay line alone, so a mid-stream retune stays continuous in the signal but can step the output audibly. |

### RollingStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingstats }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L645)

A tap rather than a filter: every sample passes through unchanged, and the window's [`mean`](math.md#autodiff-kt--mean), `variance`, `stdDev` and the current sample's [`zScore`](math.md#timeseries-kt--rollingstats--zscore) are left behind for you to read. Drop it anywhere in a `then` chain to find out what the signal is doing at that point without disturbing it.
