| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingstats--zscore"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">zScore</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L663) | How many standard deviations the sample just pushed sits from [`mean`](math.md#autodiff-kt--mean) — signed, and 0 whenever `stdDev` is 0. Note the sample is itself in the window it is being compared against. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingstats--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L667) | Records `value` into the window, refreshes all four statistics, and hands `value` straight back. |

### RollingExponentialStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingexponentialstats }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingExponentialStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L705)

Fits an exponential distribution to the last `windowSize` samples by moment matching (`lambda = 1 / mean`) and reports where the newest sample falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor. While the fitted mean or rate is at or below this the fit is abandoned rather than dividing by something near zero. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--mean"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L719) | Mean of the window after negative clamping — the only statistic an exponential fit needs. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--lambda"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lambda</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L722) | Fitted rate `1 / mean`, or 0 while the window mean is at or below `epsilon`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--variance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L725) | Variance *of the fitted distribution*, `1 / lambda²` — not the sample variance of the window. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--stddev"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L728) | Square root of `variance`, so also `1 / lambda`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L731) | `P(X <= x)` under the fit for the sample just pushed, in `0..1`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--tailprobability"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L737) | `P(X >= x) = 1 - cdf` for the sample just pushed: small means a surprisingly large sample. Sits at 1 during the degenerate case, so a silent signal reports nothing as unusual. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--clippednegativecount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L743) | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero so far. Anything but 0 means the exponential is the wrong model for this signal — take `abs()` first, or use [`RollingBetaStats`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingbetastats). |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingexponentialstats--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L754) | Clamps `value` to `>= 0`, refits the window, updates `cdf` and `tailProbability` — and returns the original `value`, clamping and all left behind in the fit. |

### ExponentialNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-exponentialnormalizer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ExponentialNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L793)

Rescales a non-negative stream by *rank* rather than by magnitude: each sample's fitted exponential CDF, mapped onto `targetMin..targetMax`. What you want when an unbounded intensity has to drive something that expects a bounded control value, and "big for this signal lately" matters more than the units.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialnormalizer--targetmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialnormalizer--targetmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialnormalizer--stats"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L805) | The fit doing the work — read `stats.lambda`, `stats.tailProbability` or `stats.clippedNegativeCount` to see what the normaliser is basing its answer on. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialnormalizer--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L808) | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### ExponentialEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-exponentialeventdetector }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ExponentialEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L826)

Fires when a sample is improbably large for the exponential distribution the preceding window fits — an onset / spike detector for non-negative streams, in the same family as [`ZScoreEventDetector`](math.md#timeseries-kt-zscoreeventdetector) but thresholding tail probability instead of standard deviations.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing can fire until this many have arrived. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--tailprobabilitythreshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire when the sample's upper-tail probability falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the top 1% of the fitted distribution". Clamped into `0..1` on use. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--influence"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample is written into the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit entirely, 1 lets them recalibrate it so a sustained shift stops being news. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor — while the window mean is at or below this, no events are reported at all. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--isevent"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L850) | Whether the most recent sample fired — the same news as a nonzero return from [`invoke`](workspace.md#stdlib-collections-kt--invoke). |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--tailprobability"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L853) | Upper-tail probability of the most recent sample; 1 during warm-up and while the fit is degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--lambda"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lambda</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L856) | Fitted exponential rate `1 / mean` over the window, or 0 while degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--clippednegativecount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L859) | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero — anything but 0 means the wrong model for this signal. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--exponentialeventdetector--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L867) | `1f` if `value` is an event, `0f` otherwise — including for every sample of the warm-up. |

### RollingGammaStats { #timeseries-kt-rollinggammastats }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingGammaStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L923)

Fits a gamma distribution to the last `windowSize` samples by matching mean and variance (`shape = mean²/variance`, `scale = variance/mean`) and reports where the newest sample falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor for the window's mean and variance, and the lower bound clamped onto the fitted shape and scale. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--mean"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L934) | Arithmetic mean of the window after negative clamping — half of the moment-matching fit. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--variance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L937) | Sample (n−1) variance of the window — a genuine sample statistic here, and the other half of the fit. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--stddev"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L940) | Square root of `variance`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--shape"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">shape</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L946) | Fitted gamma shape `mean²/variance` (the `k` parameter): 1 would be an exponential, larger is more symmetric. 0 while the fit is degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--scale"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">scale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L949) | Fitted gamma scale `variance/mean` (the `θ` parameter), in the units of your signal. 0 while degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L952) | `P(X <= x)` under the fit for the sample just pushed, in `0..1`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--tailprobability"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L955) | `1 - cdf`: the share of the fitted distribution lying above the current sample. Small means surprisingly large. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--clippednegativecount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L958) | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero — anything but 0 means a gamma is the wrong model here. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollinggammastats--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L969) | Clamps `value` to `>= 0`, re-matches shape and scale over the window, updates `cdf` and `tailProbability`, and returns the original `value` untouched. |

### GammaNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-gammanormalizer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GammaNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1009)

Rescales a non-negative, skewed stream onto `targetMin..targetMax` by its fitted gamma CDF — the two-parameter sibling of [`ExponentialNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-exponentialnormalizer), and the better pick whenever the signal's bulk sits somewhere away from zero rather than hugging it.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammanormalizer--targetmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammanormalizer--targetmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammanormalizer--stats"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1018) | The fit doing the work — read `stats.shape` and `stats.scale` to see what distribution the answers came from. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammanormalizer--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1021) | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### GammaEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-gammaeventdetector }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">GammaEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1039)

Fires when a sample lands in the upper tail of the gamma distribution the preceding window fits. The general-purpose distribution-aware onset detector in this file: it copes with the skewed, non-negative streams — magnitudes, energies, `abs()` of a motion signal — where a z-score's assumption of symmetry makes it over-fire on the low side. This is the detector the published signal examples page (`spectral_examples`) reaches for.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--tailprobabilitythreshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire when the sample's upper-tail probability falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the top 1% of the fitted distribution". Clamped into `0..1` on use. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--influence"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit, 1 lets them recalibrate it. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor for the window's mean and variance — below it, no events are reported. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--isevent"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1060) | Whether the most recent sample fired. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1063) | `P(X <= x)` of the most recent sample under the fit; 0 during warm-up and while degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--tailprobability"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1066) | `1 - cdf` for the most recent sample — the quantity actually compared with `tailProbabilityThreshold`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--shape"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">shape</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1069) | Fitted gamma shape over the window, or 0 while the fit is degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--scale"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">scale</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1072) | Fitted gamma scale over the window, in the units of your signal, or 0 while degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--clippednegativecount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1075) | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero — anything but 0 means the wrong model for this signal. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--gammaeventdetector--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1083) | `1f` if `value` is an event, `0f` otherwise — including for every sample of the warm-up. |

### RollingBetaStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingbetastats }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingBetaStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1148)

Fits a beta distribution to the last `windowSize` samples by moment matching and reports where the newest one falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--supportmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Bottom of your signal's assumed range; anything below maps to 0 and counts as clipped. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--supportmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Top of your signal's assumed range; anything above maps to 1 and counts as clipped. Must be strictly greater than `supportMin` at construction. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How far inside the open interval `(0, 1)` stored samples are held, and the degeneracy floor for the moment fit. Defaults to 1e-4, looser than the other fits in this file. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--mean"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1169) | Mean of the window in *normalised* `0..1` units, not in the units of your signal. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--variance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1172) | Sample (n−1) variance of the window, also in normalised units. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--stddev"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1175) | Square root of `variance`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--alpha"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1178) | Fitted beta `α`, the shape pulling mass toward 1; 0 when the fit fell back to min/max normalisation. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--beta"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1181) | Fitted beta `β`, the shape pulling mass toward 0; 0 when the fit fell back to min/max normalisation. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1187) | `P(X <= x)` under the fit for the sample just pushed, in `0..1` — or, when the fit is degenerate, simply that sample's normalised position within the support. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--tailprobabilitylow"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityLow</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1190) | Lower-tail probability of the current sample; equal to `cdf`. Small means unusually low for this window. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--tailprobabilityhigh"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityHigh</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1193) | Upper-tail probability of the current sample, `1 - cdf`. Small means unusually high. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--clippedtosupportcount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedToSupportCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1199) | How many samples have fallen outside `supportMin..supportMax` and been clipped into it. A count that keeps climbing means the support is wrong. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--normalizedvalue"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">normalizedValue</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1205) | The sample just pushed, mapped onto `0..1` across the support — clipped there but *before* the epsilon nudge, so unlike the value stored in the window this one can be exactly 0 or 1. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingbetastats--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1217) | Normalises `value` into the support, refits the window, updates the CDF and both tails, and returns the original `value` unchanged. |

### BetaNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-betanormalizer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BetaNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1269)

Rescales a bounded stream onto `targetMin..targetMax` by its fitted beta CDF — histogram equalisation with a two-parameter distribution standing in for the histogram. Where [`RollingNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingnormalizer) merely stretches the window's extremes apart, this spreads samples out according to how they are actually distributed, so a signal that spends its life bunched in one corner of its range comes out using the whole target range.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betanormalizer--targetmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betanormalizer--targetmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betanormalizer--stats"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1283) | The fit doing the work. Also where the support lives after construction — and where `clippedToSupportCount` will tell you the support is wrong. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betanormalizer--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1291) | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### BetaEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-betaeventdetector }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BetaEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lowerTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">upperTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1310)

A two-sided event detector for a bounded stream: it fires both when a sample is improbably high for the window's fitted beta and when it is improbably low, and the sign of the output says which. `-1f` for a lower-tail event, `+1f` for an upper-tail one, `0f` for nothing — including for the whole `windowSize`-sample warm-up.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--supportmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Bottom of your signal's assumed range; anything below is clipped to it and counted. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--supportmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">supportMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Top of your signal's assumed range; must be strictly greater than `supportMin` at construction. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--lowertailthreshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lowerTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire low when the CDF falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the bottom 1% of the fit". Clamped into `0..1`; set above 0.5 and nearly everything becomes an event. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--uppertailthreshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">upperTailThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire high when `1 - cdf` falls to this or below — the top 1% at 0.01. Clamped into `0..1`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--influence"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit, 1 lets a sustained shift recalibrate it. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Boundary nudge for stored samples and degeneracy floor for the moment fit; 1e-4 by default. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--isevent"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1337) | Whether the most recent sample fired at either end. It does not say which end — the sign of [`invoke`](workspace.md#stdlib-collections-kt--invoke)'s return does. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1340) | CDF of the most recent sample under the fit, or its normalised position when degenerate; parked at 0.5 during warm-up. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--alpha"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1343) | Fitted beta `α` over the window; 0 when the fit fell back to plain normalisation. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--beta"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">beta</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1346) | Fitted beta `β` over the window; 0 when the fit fell back to plain normalisation. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--clippedtosupportcount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedToSupportCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1349) | How many samples have been clipped into `supportMin..supportMax` — a climbing count means the support is wrong. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--betaeventdetector--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1361) | `-1f` for a lower-tail event, `+1f` for an upper-tail one, `0f` for neither and for the whole warm-up. If both thresholds somehow fire at once, the lower tail wins. |

### RollingRayleighStats { #timeseries-kt-rollingrayleighstats }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingRayleighStats</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1430)

Fits a Rayleigh distribution to the last `windowSize` samples and reports where the newest one falls within it. A tap: the sample passes through unchanged.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | How many samples the fit sees. Must be `>= 2`; the ring buffer is allocated up front. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor on the window's second moment and on `sigma` — below it, nothing is reported. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--sigma"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sigma</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1441) | Fitted Rayleigh scale, `sqrt(mean(x²) / 2)`; 0 while the window's second moment is at or below `epsilon`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--mean"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mean</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1444) | Mean *of the fitted distribution*, `sigma * sqrt(π/2)` — derived from `sigma`, not averaged from the window. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--variance"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">variance</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1447) | Variance of the fitted distribution, `((4 - π)/2) * sigma²`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--stddev"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDev</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1450) | Square root of `variance`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1453) | `P(X <= x) = 1 - exp(-x² / 2sigma²)` for the sample just pushed. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--tailprobability"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1456) | `1 - cdf`: the share of the fitted distribution above the current sample. Small means a surprisingly large magnitude. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--clippednegativecount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1462) | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero. A magnitude should never be negative, so anything but 0 means the wrong signal is arriving here. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingrayleighstats--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1473) | Clamps `value` to `>= 0`, re-estimates `sigma` from the window's second moment, updates the fitted moments and the CDF, and returns the original `value` unchanged. |

### RayleighNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-rayleighnormalizer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RayleighNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1512)

Rescales a stream of magnitudes onto `targetMin..targetMax` by its fitted Rayleigh CDF. The one to use when the numbers arriving are lengths of 2-D vectors — cursor speed, optical-flow magnitude, gradient strength — because a single-parameter fit adapts on far less history than [`GammaNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-gammanormalizer) needs.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleighnormalizer--targetmin"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 0 maps to. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleighnormalizer--targetmax"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The value a CDF of 1 maps to. May be set below `targetMin` to invert the mapping. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleighnormalizer--stats"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">stats</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1521) | The fit doing the work — `stats.sigma` is the single number the whole mapping rests on. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleighnormalizer--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1524) | Pushes `value` through the fit and returns its CDF mapped into `targetMin..targetMax`. |

### RayleighEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-rayleigheventdetector }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RayleighEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="nc">DISTRIBUTION&#95;EPSILON</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1540)

Fires when a magnitude is improbably large for the Rayleigh distribution the preceding window fits. The detector to pair with a speed or vector-length signal: a sudden lunge, a flick, a burst of optical flow.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the fit. Must be `>= 2`, and nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--tailprobabilitythreshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbabilityThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Fire when the sample's upper-tail probability falls to this or below — at 0.01, "in the top 1% of the fitted distribution". Clamped into `0..1` on use. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--influence"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, `0..1` (clamped): 0 keeps events out of the fit, 1 lets them recalibrate it. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--epsilon"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Degeneracy floor on the window's second moment and on `sigma` — below it, no events are reported. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--isevent"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1561) | Whether the most recent sample fired. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--sigma"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sigma</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1564) | Fitted Rayleigh scale over the window, `sqrt(mean(x²) / 2)`, or 0 while degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--cdf"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">cdf</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1567) | `P(X <= x)` of the most recent sample under the fit; 0 during warm-up and while degenerate. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--tailprobability"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">tailProbability</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1570) | `1 - cdf` for the most recent sample — the quantity compared with `tailProbabilityThreshold`. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--clippednegativecount"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clippedNegativeCount</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Long</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1573) | How many negative samples have been clamped to zero; a magnitude should never be negative. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rayleigheventdetector--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1581) | `1f` if `value` is an event, `0f` otherwise — including for every sample of the warm-up. |

### ZScoreEventDetector { #timeseries-kt-zscoreeventdetector }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">ZScoreEventDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1641)

The classic smoothed z-score peak detector: it fires when the newest sample sits more than [`threshold`](imaging.md#imaging-kt--threshold) standard deviations from the mean of the window, and its output carries the direction — `+1f` above, `-1f` below, `0f` for no event and throughout the warm-up.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--zscoreeventdetector--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the mean and standard deviation; nothing fires until this many have arrived. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--zscoreeventdetector--threshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How many standard deviations from the window mean counts as an event — 3 to 4 is a conventional starting point. The test is strict and on `\|z\|`, so it fires in both directions. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--zscoreeventdetector--influence"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">influence</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How much of an event's own sample enters the window, nominally `0..1` but **not** clamped: 0 substitutes the previous sample, so a sustained level shift keeps being reported forever, while 1 lets the detector adapt to it and fall silent. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--zscoreeventdetector--isevent"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isEvent</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1661) | Whether the most recent sample fired, in either direction. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--zscoreeventdetector--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1668) | `+1f` or `-1f` for an event above or below the window, `0f` for none — and `0f` for the first `windowSize` samples while the window fills, and whenever the window is perfectly flat. |

### AdaptiveCompander { #timeseries-kt-adaptivecompander }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AdaptiveCompander</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.5f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isCompressor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1717)

An envelope follower plus a static gain curve: it either squashes the loud parts toward [`threshold`](imaging.md#imaging-kt--threshold) (compressor) or pushes the quiet parts further down (expander), depending on [`isCompressor`](math.md#timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--iscompressor). Everything is in linear units, which makes this the plain, cheap sibling of [`DynamicRangeCompressor`](math.md#timeseries-kt-dynamicrangecompressor) — that one does the same job in dB, with a soft knee and real attack and release times.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--attack"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used while the envelope is *rising*; larger reacts faster to a growing signal. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--release"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used while the envelope is *falling*; larger lets the gain recover faster after a peak. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--threshold"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The linear amplitude where the curve bends — above it for a compressor, below it for an expander. Not dB. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--ratio"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How hard the curve bends: as a compressor the excess above [`threshold`](imaging.md#imaging-kt--threshold) is divided by this; as an expander the shortfall below it is multiplied by it. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--iscompressor"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">isCompressor</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | `true` compresses (pull the loud parts in), `false` expands (push the quiet parts down). Switchable mid-stream. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivecompander--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1735) | Updates the envelope from `abs(value)` and returns `value` scaled by the gain the curve asks for at that envelope. |

### AGC { #timeseries-kt-agc }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AGC</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetLevel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">1.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.001f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxGain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">10.0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1776)

Automatic gain control: follows the signal's envelope and scales the signal so that envelope sits at [`targetLevel`](math.md#timeseries-kt--agc--targetlevel). Reach for it when you care about the *shape* of a signal whose absolute scale you cannot predict — a sensor whose range depends on how it was mounted, a control stream you want to hand to something expecting `0..1`.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--agc--targetlevel"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetLevel</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | The envelope level the gain chases, in the same linear units as your signal. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--agc--attack"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used when the envelope rises and when the gain must increase; larger is faster. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--agc--release"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Per-sample coefficient (`0..1`) used when the envelope falls and when the gain must decrease. The default is ten times slower than `attack`, so the gain backs off gently. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--agc--maxgain"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">maxGain</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Ceiling on the multiplier, so a near-silent stretch cannot be amplified without limit. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--agc--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1793) | Updates the envelope and the smoothed gain, then returns `value` multiplied by that gain. |

### LeakyIntegrator { #timeseries-kt-leakyintegrator }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">LeakyIntegrator</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">leakRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.99f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1825)

A running sum that forgets: `sum = sum * leakRate + value`. The signal-processing way to ask "how much has been going on lately" — feed it event flags or rectified magnitudes and it climbs with activity, then decays back down when things go quiet.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--leakyintegrator--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1828) | Leaks the accumulator once, adds `value`, and returns the new total. Starts from 0 and has no reset. |

### RollingNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-rollingnormalizer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMin</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">targetMax</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1847)

Stretches the last `windowSize` samples onto `targetMin..targetMax` using their own minimum and maximum — the simplest auto-ranging there is, and the one to use when you know nothing about the signal's distribution and just need something bounded. Note the default target is `-1..1`, not `0..1`.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingnormalizer--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1856) | Records `value`, then returns it rescaled from the window's current min..max onto `targetMin..targetMax` — or the midpoint of that range while the window is flat. |

### RollingOneDollarNormalizer { #timeseries-kt-rollingonedollarnormalizer }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">RollingOneDollarNormalizer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1885)

Centres the stream on its window mean and divides by the largest absolute deviation in that window, so the output lands in `-1..1` with `±1` reached exactly by whichever sample is currently furthest from the mean. A symmetric, zero-centred alternative to [`RollingNormalizer`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingnormalizer): "which side of typical" stays meaningful, at the price of letting one outlier set the scale for a whole window.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--rollingonedollarnormalizer--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1894) | Records `value` and returns its deviation from the window mean divided by the window's largest absolute deviation; 0 while the window is constant. |

### AdaptiveThresholder { #timeseries-kt-adaptivethresholder }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">AdaptiveThresholder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDevMultiplier</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">2.0f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clamp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1931)

Despite the name this returns a continuous value, not a decision: the sample's distance from the window mean, measured in units of [`stdDevMultiplier`](math.md#timeseries-kt--adaptivethresholder--stddevmultiplier) standard deviations. A sample sitting exactly `stdDevMultiplier` sigma above the mean comes out as `+1`, and it is thresholding that downstream — or a [`SchmittTrigger`](math.md#timeseries-kt-schmitttrigger) — that turns it into a decision.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivethresholder--windowsize"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span></code> | Samples of history behind the mean and standard deviation. The buffer is allocated up front. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivethresholder--stddevmultiplier"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">stdDevMultiplier</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | How many standard deviations map to an output of 1. Larger is a gentler scale. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivethresholder--clamp"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">clamp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span></code> | Coerce the output into `-1..1` instead of letting it run past the ends. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--adaptivethresholder--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1947) | Records `value` and returns its deviation from the window mean divided by `stdDev * stdDevMultiplier`, optionally clamped to `-1..1`. |

### DerivativeFilter { #timeseries-kt-derivativefilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">DerivativeFilter</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L1982)

First difference: this sample minus the previous one. The cheapest way to turn something position-shaped into something velocity-shaped, or to find the edges in a slow signal.

### IntegralFilter { #timeseries-kt-integralfilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nc">IntegralFilter</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2001)

### DCBlocker { #timeseries-kt-dcblocker }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DCBlocker</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">r</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.995f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2022)

Removes whatever constant offset a signal is riding on, without waiting for a window to fill: a one-pole, one-zero high-pass, `y = x - x₋₁ + r·y₋₁`, parked just above DC. The standard thing to put at the head of a chain when you care how a sensor is *changing* rather than where its zero happens to sit.

### PeakDetector { #timeseries-kt-peakdetector }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PeakDetector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">decay</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.99f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2045)

A peak-hold envelope: it jumps instantly to `abs(value)` whenever that exceeds the current peak, and otherwise decays toward zero by a factor of `decay` each sample. What you want for a level meter, a "how hard was that hit" reading, or the denominator of a hand-rolled normaliser.

### SchmittTrigger { #timeseries-kt-schmitttrigger }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">SchmittTrigger</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">lowThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">highThreshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2068)

A comparator with hysteresis: it goes high once the input rises above `highThreshold` and only comes back down once the input falls below `lowThreshold`, so a signal loitering around a single threshold cannot chatter. Returns `1f` while high and `0f` while low.

### MedianFilter { #timeseries-kt-medianfilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">MedianFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2093)

Rolling median of the last `windowSize` samples. The spike killer: unlike any moving average it removes an isolated outlier completely instead of spreading it over its neighbourhood, and it leaves real edges where they are instead of smearing them into ramps.

### NoiseGate { #timeseries-kt-noisegate }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">NoiseGate</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">threshold</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attack</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">release</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.1f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2124)

Passes the signal through untouched while it is loud enough and hard-zeroes it when it is not. The gate opens when the tracked envelope rises above `threshold` and closes only once the envelope falls below *half* that, so a signal hovering at the threshold does not flutter.

### PIDController { #timeseries-kt-pidcontroller }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PIDController</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kp</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ki</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kd</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2158)

A textbook proportional-integral-derivative controller wired up as a filter: it reads the *measured* value and returns the control effort that should push it toward [`setpoint`](math.md#timeseries-kt--pidcontroller--setpoint). In a box this is what to reach for when one thing should chase another — a camera trailing a target, a value easing toward the mouse — with overshoot you get to tune rather than inherit.

### CooldownFilter { #timeseries-kt-cooldownfilter }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">CooldownFilter</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">cooldownSamples</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2185)
