### StreamingWhitener { #timeseries-kt-streamingwhitener }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">StreamingWhitener</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.01f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">epsilon</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">1e</span><span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">5f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2214)

A z-score with no window: it tracks the mean and the variance exponentially and returns how far the current sample sits from that running mean, in running standard deviations. The O(1)-memory alternative to [`RollingStats`](math.md#timeseries-kt-rollingstats) plus arithmetic, and the natural pre-stage for anything that wants a roughly zero-mean, unit-variance input.

### BimodalThresholder { #timeseries-kt-bimodalthresholder }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">BimodalThresholder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">alpha</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mf">0.05f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">interpolate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">false</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2258)

Online two-means clustering of a stream: it keeps two centroids, moves whichever is nearer toward each new sample, and reports which of the two the sample joined. For a signal that really does live at two levels — a switch, a contact sensor, a light that is on or off, a gesture held or not — this finds the two levels for you instead of making you guess a threshold, and it follows them as they drift.

| Declaration | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--bimodalthresholder--invoke"></a>[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">override</span> <span class="k">fun</span> <span class="nf">invoke</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">value</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2267) | `-1f` or `+1f` for the lower or upper cluster — or the interpolated position between the centroids when `interpolate` is set — and `0f` until both centroids have been seeded. |

### PercentileThresholder { #timeseries-kt-percentilethresholder }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">PercentileThresholder</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">val</span> <span class="n">windowSize</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Int</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">mapToMinusOneToOne</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Boolean</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="kc">true</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2322)

Reports where the current sample ranks within the last `windowSize` samples: the fraction of the *rest* of the window lying strictly below it. (The current sample is in the window but can never count itself, so the denominator is one less than the fill level and a new high reads exactly 1.0.) Completely distribution-free — no mean, no standard deviation, no fitted law — so a heavy-tailed or lopsided signal cannot mislead it, and one wild outlier moves the output by exactly one rank.

### DynamicRangeCompressor { #timeseries-kt-dynamicrangecompressor }

[<code class="highlight"><span class="k">class</span> <span class="nf">DynamicRangeCompressor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">thresholdDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="p">-</span><span class="mi">20f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">ratio</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">4f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">kneeWidthDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">10f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">attackMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">5f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">releaseMs</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">50f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">sampleRate</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">44100f</span><span class="p">,</span> <span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">makeupGainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span> <span class="o">=</span> <span class="mi">0f</span><span class="p">)</span> <span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">FloatFilter</span></code>](source/jvmMain/afield/math/statistics/timeseries/#L2368)

A proper dB-domain compressor: envelope follower, soft knee, attack and release in milliseconds, makeup gain. Where [`AdaptiveCompander`](math.md#timeseries-kt-adaptivecompander) works in linear amplitude with per-sample coefficients, this one is specified the way a compressor usually is, which makes it the one to use on anything audio-shaped, or on anything whose timing you would rather state in milliseconds than in samples.

Negative values are the norm. |

The 44100 default is an audio assumption — set it to your frame rate for a control signal. |
| <a id="timeseries-kt--dynamicrangecompressor--makeupgaindb"></a><code class="highlight"><span class="k">var</span> <span class="n">makeupGainDb</span><span class="p">:</span> <span class="nc">Float</span></code> | Flat gain (dB) applied after the compression, to win back the headroom it just took. Applied at all levels, reduction or not. |

## units.kt { #units-kt }

Physical units for Field's spreadsheet-style numbers. A [`Quantity`](math.md#units-kt-quantity) pairs a KotUniL
`Expression` (normalized to SI) with the display unit the user actually wrote, so `3 | mm`
still prints as "3 mm".

[`withUnit`](math.md#units-kt--withunit) is what that `| unit` syntax lowers to, and the operator overloads here let a
[`Quantity`](math.md#units-kt-quantity) mix with plain `Number`s and bare `Expression`s in either order under ordinary
dimensional-analysis rules. The rest of the file is presentation: [`recognizeDerivedUnit`](math.md#units-kt--recognizederivedunit)
matches a dimensional signature against a table of named SI derived units (N, J, W, Pa, Hz, V,
Ω, ...), [`autoScaleExpression`](math.md#units-kt--autoscaleexpression) chooses an SI prefix, and [`formatUnitSuperscripts`](math.md#units-kt--formatunitsuperscripts) rewrites
`kg*m2/s2` as `kg·m²/s²`. [`formatExpression`](math.md#units-kt--formatexpression) runs those in that order.

The unit algebra itself is KotUniL's, not Field's. Two limits are visible in the code: only
single-factor dimensions are auto-scaled (compound ones like m/s pass through unchanged), and
the derived-unit table is a fixed list, so anything outside it falls back to raw SI symbols.

`src/jvmMain/kotlin/afield/math/units/units.kt` — [read the source](source/jvmMain/afield/math/units/units/)
